newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude rebounds on technicals to end higher.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude rebounds on technicals to end higher.

text.p: NYMEX crude ended higher after staging a late session rally Tuesday on short covering and technical strength ahead of weekly oil inventory data.

"We were able to hold the (technical support) numbers today and that's what took us up. But, fundamentally nothing has changed," said Michael Busby, trader with Northville Industries in Melville, New York.

April crude settled up 41 cents at $20.66 a barrel. Oil prices have lost more than 20 percent in the last month due to refiners cutting crude usage to make seasonal repairs while mild winter temperatures have slackened heating oil demand.
In the morning, spot crude fell 17 cents to $20.08 but rebounded from support confirmed Monday that lay about $20.00 and headed higher, forcing shorts to cover, dealers said.
Some dealers said a major player has been selling front crude months to buy back months the last two sessions, but they said the spread play was not seen today, allowing crude to rise unimpeded.

April gasoline ended up 1.12 cents a gallon at 62.89 cents, and April heating oil finished 0.16 cent higher at 53.34 cents a gallon. Prompt heating oil earlier held key trendline support drawn from the spot low in April 1995.

Most traders expected this evening's weekly oil inventory report by the American Petroleum Institute (API) to show a slight build in gasoline stocks, but some said refiner de-stocking and strong demand could lead to a surprise decline.
Indeed, the report said gasoline stocks dropped 1.3 million barrels with implied demand at a seasonally strong eight million barrels a day.
The report in general defied expectations.

Crude stocks unexpectedly dropped 7.6 million barrels when traders anticipated a build of near three million. Distillate stocks, which include heating oil and diesel, rose 603,000 barrels when traders had expected a seasonal draw of one to to two million barrels.
Kuwaiti Crown Prince and Prime Minister Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah was taken to hospital on Tuesday for medical tests following a sudden health problem.
Kuwait, one of the world's leading oil producers, is part of the 11-member Organization for Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC).

"It has very little to do with the (oil) price rise today," said Ed Kevelson, director of refined products for Paribas Futures Inc in New York. Kuwaiti officials said Sheikh Saad was in good condition.
It was not immediately clear what Sheikh Saad, born in 1930, was suffering from but one Western diplomatic source said there were indications he was in good condition.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
